links.note: Cannot read the blackboard from the last row, corrected with a concave lens - myopia (245).
Least distance of distinct vision is 25 cm - the near point (244), not accommodation itself (243).
The reddish morning Sun is explained by scattering, with the answer building the 1/lambda^4 argument (257). 259 is the sky's blue, and 260 the danger-signal case; neither is what is asked.
Same blackboard case with a ray diagram for the correction - myopia and its concave lens (245).
Seeing both near and distant objects clearly is the power of accommodation (243); the near and far points (244) are its limits, not the mechanism asked for.
A star's apparent position differs from its true one because the atmosphere's layers bend its light - atmospheric refraction (253). 254 would be the flicker, not the displacement.
Names the two common defects, myopia and hypermetropia. Filed on 245 as the first named; the item spans 245 and 246 equally.
Concave-lens spectacles mean myopia (245).
Convex-lens spectacles mean hypermetropia (246).
Diagram of the colours thrown on a white screen by a prism - dispersion (250). 251 would be naming the seven colours; here the splitting is what is drawn.
Short-sightedness defined with its causes (elongated eyeball, over-curved cornea) and correction - myopia (245).
Long-sightedness with its causes and correction - hypermetropia (246).
An elderly person failing at both distances and needing bifocals - presbyopia (247), not hypermetropia (246).
A rainbow seen in fountain spray with the Sun behind - water droplets acting as prisms (252), which is dispersion applied in the sky rather than dispersion itself (250).
A myopic person sees only nearby objects clearly (245).
Long-sightedness needs a convex lens of a definite focal length - hypermetropia and its correction (246).
The noon Sun looks white because its light travels the shortest path and is least scattered (257).
Sees distant but not near objects - all three names in the options are hypermetropia (246).
Cannot see distant objects but sees nearby ones - myopia (245), against hypermetropia and presbyopia as distractors.
The black opening between aqueous humour and lens is the pupil - eye structure (242).
